title: [D2 Context] Entity extraction with observation-scoped traffic
summary: The signal layer's second output exists: sql/migrations/0007_context_entities.sql creates helena_signal_entity_observations (a plain view, one row per flow-and-entity observation) and helena_signal_context_entities (a materialized view, one row per entity per context). Address, domain, fingerprint and url entities are extracted from the places concept/05-threat-intelligence.md names, each row carries five flags saying which layer observed the value and the bidirectional traffic of the distinct flows that observed it, and context_id and aggregation_version are read off the host context rather than recomputed.
assumption_validated: That the join target the enrichment tier needs can be produced entirely in the engine, at one row per entity per context, without losing what the composition rule turns on. It can: RisingWave 3.0.3 accepts a nine-branch UNION ALL feeding a TUMBLE over a plain view, two levels of GROUP BY in one streaming plan, bool_or as a streaming aggregate, and an equi-join from that aggregate to the host-context materialized view. Over the ten-record layer fixture and again over all 62 sampled records, every entity row matches the same row rebuilt from the JSON in Python -- key, five flags, flow count and four counters. The scope distinction survives on real data: 16 of the 30 addresses that appear as A answers in the sample are never a flow destination, and their flag says so. The domain limitation concept/02 records is confirmed rather than solved -- a name still carries the traffic of the flows that mentioned it, and the four layer flags are what the rendering gets instead.
makes_buildable: The enrichment join (D3) has its join target: helena_signal_context_entities, with entity_type telling a feed which rows are its, entity_value the value as observed, and fingerprint_algorithm separating a JA3 (one source, so no_match is reachable) from a JA4 (no source at all, so missing is the only honest state). The enriched-context view can now be written reading helena_signal_host_context and helena_signal_context_entities and nothing below them. The ThreatFox loader's ip:port split has bare-address rows to match against, and its domain rows have names as observed. The triage rendering has the per-domain and per-address records concept/03-architecture.md says it needs, with the traffic beside each one, and prd task 15 (registrable-domain normalization) has one place to apply itself: the domain branch of helena_signal_entity_observations.

verification.detail: 514 passed in 585s, whole suite, against a real RisingWave 3.0.3 started from bin/. Every assertion about the new views executes SQL against a throwaway schema on that engine over records put through the real normalizer -- nothing asserts on SQL text. 70 of the 514 are tests/test_context.py, 16 of them new. Two extraction branches no sampled record can reach (a URI with userinfo, a port and a fragment; a relative URI) are demonstrated with a real record whose URI string was replaced in a tmp_path capture, which is the technique tasks 12 and 13 established. The per-flow deduplication was mutation-checked outside the suite: with the inner aggregation removed, ocsp.digicert.com reads 2 flows / 1544 octets instead of 1 / 772, so test_an_entity_observed_twice_on_one_flow_counts_that_flow_once discriminates.

invariant_conflicts.detail: How many entity types there are. concept/02-concepts-and-taxonomy.md's glossary defines an entity as 'a `domain`, an `address`, or a TLS `fingerprint`' -- three. concept/05-threat-intelligence.md's 'What can be enriched' table has four, adding `url` extracted from HTTP and HTTP/2 URIs, and prd task 14 lists four. Four are implemented, because 05 is the specific note about what enrichment joins to, it names the source of every one of the four, and the url gap it records ('URL feeds have narrow reach ... TLS yields SNI, not a URL') only makes sense if url rows exist. The glossary line in 02 looks like an omission rather than a decision, but correcting concept/ is the operator's call, not a session's.

deferred: Normalizing a domain: nothing is lowercased and no registrable domain is derived. That is prd task 15 (the Public Suffix List), and ADR-0009 already fixes the matching rule for one source -- match on the name as observed, never on the registrable domain. Measured: no DNS name, SNI or URI host in the sample carries an uppercase character, so case folding today would be unexercised guessing.

An opaque entity id. The natural key (context_id, entity_type, entity_value) is unique, asserted, and is what a citation would carry; a digest over three columns that are already on the row is a second identifier for the same thing. The increment that issues a citation is where one would earn its place.

A CNAME's target as a domain entity of its own. concept/05 lists DNS response names and that is what is taken. Measured: the sample's 46 CNAME records carry 29 distinct targets and every one also appears as the name of another resource record, so nothing is lost on this input; a chain ending in a CNAME to a name no record is then about would lose that name, and the migration says so.
The server's fingerprints. concept/05 says JA3 and JA4 client-side only, so ja3s/ja4s produce no entity row -- asserted absent from entity_value rather than assumed.
A per-entity duration. The task's traffic columns are flows, packets and octets, and nothing above reads a per-entity duration.

A decision record under docs/. The extraction rules, the observation-scoped traffic, the flags, the coverage gaps and the URI host expression are argued in the head of sql/migrations/0007_context_entities.sql, which is where a reader of the SQL looks; prds/CONTEXT.md §5 asks not to grow docs/ where the code and the report carry it. Same choice task 13 made.
lessons: task 14: RisingWave 3.0.3 takes the whole entity construction in one streaming plan -- measured, not inferred: bool_or works as a streaming aggregate (in a plain view and in an MV), a GROUP BY over a subquery that itself has a GROUP BY is accepted, TUMBLE over a plain view whose body is a nine-branch UNION ALL joined to another view works, and an equi-join from that aggregate to an existing materialized view (helena_signal_host_context) is accepted and returns rows. The 0002 measurement that a CROSS JOIN is rejected as a 'streaming nested-loop join' does NOT extend to an equi-join -- do not re-derive the whole design around that.

task 14: A second TUMBLE means a second copy of INTERVAL '5 minutes', because TUMBLE takes a named relation and the two views window different ones. The way to make that safe without editing an applied migration is to take context_id and aggregation_version off the host-context row through the join instead of recomputing them, and to assert that every entity row joins a context AND that the window ENDS agree. A drifted interval then breaks the join rather than producing plausible wrong rows.

task 14: Put the window's TUMBLE over a plain intermediate view rather than in each branch of a union. The intermediate (helena_signal_entity_observations) also gives the reconciliation test something to count -- one row per extracted value per flow, computed from the JSON in Python -- which is where a join key that silently matches nothing would show up.

task 14: Per-entity traffic needs TWO levels of aggregation, and the inner one is not cosmetic. Mutation-checked: without it, a host mentioned by two HTTP requests on one flow reads 2 flows / 1544 octets instead of 1 / 772. Group first by (entity, flow) taking the counters with max, then by (entity, context) summing them.

task 14: `urlsplit(uri).hostname` is the right expectation to test a SQL host expression against -- it drops scheme, userinfo, port, path, query and fragment in one call -- but it lowercases where the SQL does not. That difference is invisible on this input and is the normalization deferred to task 15; a test that introduced an uppercase host would fail for the wrong reason.

task 14: The layer-coverage fixture (ace6ca33..., 10 records) reaches every extraction branch and both windows, and it contains the two cases the flags exist for: 40.126.32.138 resolved and then connected to, and six answers of the same lookup resolved and never contacted. tcp.4's two requests to one host are the real record that exercises the per-flow dedupe. Nothing had to be constructed except the two URI-shape branches.

task 14: `fingerprint_algorithm` is NULL on every row that is not a fingerprint, and that NULL is a property of the type rather than an unobserved value -- the same idiom the flatten layer already uses for HTTP/2's exchange_number. It is on the row because the enrichment join cannot otherwise keep `missing` (a JA4, which has no source at all) apart from `no_match` (a JA3 that no source matched), which concept/instruction.md §2 forbids collapsing.
failed_approaches: task 14: Nothing was tried and abandoned in the implementation. One thing worth not repeating: the engine that was running at the start of this session died on its own partway through (its log shows a SIGTERM from before the session), so a probe that connected once failed minutes later with 'connection refused'. Start a throwaway engine with an explicit pidfile rather than assuming the one that answered a moment ago is still there, and stop it at the end -- pytest's conftest reuses whatever is already answering.
next_session_should_know: The entity rows are helena_signal_context_entities in sql/migrations/0007_context_entities.sql, columns in order: context_id, tenant, sensor, host, window_start, window_end, entity_type, entity_value, fingerprint_algorithm, observed_as_flow_destination, observed_in_dns_query, observed_in_dns_response, observed_in_tls, observed_in_http, observed_flow_count, observed_bytes_sent, observed_bytes_received, observed_packets_sent, observed_packets_received, aggregation_version. tests/test_context.py::CONTEXT_ENTITIES_SHAPE is the second copy of that interface and is asserted against the engine, so adding a column means editing that tuple too -- the same deliberate friction FLATTEN_SHAPES and HOST_CONTEXT_SHAPE have. Six things to build on rather than rediscover. (1) The grain is one row per (context_id, entity_type, entity_value) and it is asserted two ways: no duplicate key, and the whole row set equal to the same set rebuilt from the JSON. (2) The traffic columns are observation-scoped -- the traffic of the flows in which the entity was observed, summed over DISTINCT flows -- and they are not traffic to the entity. Do not rename them to something that reads as if they were, and do not add a total: the four stay bidirectional. (3) The five flags are the vocabulary the rendering gets. observed_as_flow_destination is the composition rule's scope test for addresses; for domains there is no scope test and the other four flags are the weaker substitute concept/02 records, so a rendering may say 'this name was an SNI' and may not say 'this name received bytes'. (4) context_id and aggregation_version come from helena_signal_host_context through an equi-join -- there is no second digest and no second version literal in 0007, and the join is what pins the duplicated INTERVAL '5 minutes'. (5) The layering now has three objects in the signal layer and tests/test_context.py::test_every_signal_object_declares_what_it_is is a prefix query, so an object added to the layer without a declaration fails there (that test is task 13's, widened from the single host-context assertion and renamed). The analytical layer above must read helena_signal_host_context and helena_signal_context_entities and never the flatten layer or helena_normalized_events. (6) Where prd task 15 applies: the domain branch of helena_signal_entity_observations is the one place a name becomes an entity value, so registrable-domain normalization has exactly one seam -- and ADR-0009 constrains it to match on the name as observed. Untouched and still open from earlier sessions: bin/README.md's dangling reference to scripts/build-binaries.sh, and the two cross-cutting open questions in concept/08 (the record lost at a catch-up boundary, and durability for the single store).
